Reasoning: let the width of the large rectangle be W and the height be H. The perimeter of the large rectangle is 30 cm, so 2(W+H)=30, that is, W+H=15. The shaded upper-left part is a square, with area 9 cm^2, so the side length is 3 cm. Therefore the vertical dividing line is 3 cm from the left boundary, and the horizontal dividing line is 3 cm from the upper boundary. The width of the lower-right rectangle ABCD is W-3, and its height is H-3, so its perimeter is 2[(W-3)+(H-3)] = 2(W+H-6) = 2(15-6) = 18 cm.

The shaded upper-left part is a square, and rectangle ABCD is the lower-right part, with A and D on the vertical cut and B and C on the right side. From the text, the outer rectangle has perimeter 30 cm, so if its width is W and height is H, then W + H = 15. The shaded square has area 9 cm^2, so its side length is 3 cm. Because this square occupies the upper-left corner, the vertical cut is 3 cm from the left edge and the horizontal cut is 3 cm below the top edge. Therefore rectangle ABCD has dimensions W - 3 by H - 3. Its perimeter is 2[(W - 3) + (H - 3)] = 2(W + H - 6) = 2(15 - 6) = 18 cm.
